## Summary

Torch-native extend pads Query to the full KV length, computes cached-prefix Query rows, and discards their outputs. Run SDPA only for new tokens, and reuse existing CPU length/request-index mirrors to avoid scalar synchronization.

```text
before: SDPA([unused prefix Query; new Query], cached KV) → discard prefix output
after:  SDPA(new Query, cached KV, prefix-aligned causal bias) → new output
```

- Ordinary prefix causality uses PyTorch `causal_lower_right`; eligible fused CUDA dispatch is retained. Sliding-window masks use absolute Query offsets. Prefix-free causal attention retains `is_causal=True`.
- CPU mirrors are used only for non-speculative extend. Missing/length-mismatched mirrors fall back per field; no new device-to-host transfer or persistent batch state is introduced. Decode is unchanged.
- Tests separate input preparation, independent reference math, and backend execution, with public ENCODER_ONLY coverage as well as causal/cross-attention paths.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `3831e7e091` (main on 2026-10-09).

- **Before:** the query-workload regression fails on latest main; the CPU-metadata profiler regression fails on the prefix-only intermediate commit.
  **After:** **38 tests and 36 subtests pass** across the four files below. Existing host mirrors eliminate scalar extraction (ordinary prefix causal: **7 → 0** reads).
- Numerical coverage includes ragged batches, shuffled KV mapping, GQA/MHA, distinct QK/value dimensions, causal/window boundaries, encoder offsets, cross/encoder-only attention, dtype conversion, zero-extend rows, absent/unpadded mirrors, and stale speculative mirrors. SDPA executes real math, checked against independent matmul/softmax results.
- Fresh MPS FP16 validation: all **21 scenarios** (prefixes 0/512/2048/4096; causal/window/noncausal; 16 new tokens, plus 9 three-request ragged cases with 128/127/126 new tokens) match latest main exactly and pass an independent CPU float32 reference at `atol=rtol=0.002`. The 10 new test methods also pass on **PyTorch 2.13.0** as an additional compatibility check. Pre-commit passes on both changed files.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_torch_native_extend.py \
  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_local_attention.py \

  test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_kv_translate_ownership.py -q
```

### Speed Tests and Profiling

Apple M5 Pro (20-core GPU, 48 GB unified memory), macOS 27.0, PyTorch 2.14.0, MPS FP16, batch 1, 8 heads, head dimension 128, 16 new tokens. CPU operator fallback disabled; 10 warmups and 60 samples per variant, rotating execution order and synchronizing MPS before/after each sample. Latest-main paired medians:

| Mode | Cached prefix tokens | Main ms | This PR ms | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| causal | 512 | 1.537 | 0.398 | 3.86x |
| causal | 2048 | 2.223 | 0.916 | 2.43x |
| causal | 4096 | 6.613 | 2.655 | 2.49x |
| sliding_window_128 | 512 | 1.988 | 0.408 | 4.87x |
| sliding_window_128 | 2048 | 4.083 | 0.954 | 4.28x |
| sliding_window_128 | 4096 | 9.089 | 1.548 | 5.87x |
| noncausal | 512 | 1.544 | 0.304 | 5.08x |
| noncausal | 2048 | 2.559 | 0.686 | 3.73x |
| noncausal | 4096 | 5.917 | 1.402 | 4.22x |

Timing uses real ForwardBatch and public `forward_extend`, including metadata selection/CPU `tolist`, output allocation, KV gather, mask construction and SDPA. Existing batch construction, input transfer, and KV writes are excluded. Masks are constructed inside timing. These are attention-function measurements; model throughput and the MLX backend are outside this benchmark.

### CUDA validation and profiling (Google Colab, 2026-10-10)

Tesla T4 with Colab Torch 2.11.0+cu130 and A100-SXM4-40GB with the repository-pinned Torch **2.14.1+cu130**, CUDA 13.0. Same FP16 batch-1 / 8-head / dim-128 / 16-new-token / 10-warmup / 60-sample synchronized, rotating-order protocol; A100 nonzero-prefix scenarios were repeated, and its table entries use the repeated paired medians.

| GPU / Torch | Prefix tokens | Main ms | This PR ms | Speedup |

| T4 / 2.11.0+cu130 | 512 | 0.6331 | 0.3774 | 1.68x |
| T4 / 2.11.0+cu130 | 2048 | 1.9767 | 0.5570 | 3.55x |

Standalone source-isolated backend tests passed: 12 FP16 scenarios per GPU, plus 9 A100 BF16 GQA/ragged scenarios (3 requests, 8 Q / 2 KV heads, 128/127/126 new tokens). Fixed backend method bodies and ForwardBatch dataclass/enum definitions were loaded without importing the unrelated serving stack; unused base/mixin scaffolding was excluded, and KV buffers used real tensors. Checks compare baseline outputs and an independent CPU FP32 reference (FP16 atol/rtol=0.002; BF16=0.01). Maximum baseline difference: T4 FP16 0, A100 FP16 0.00024414, A100 BF16 0.00097656. These are backend-function checks, not full serving/model integration tests.

Profiler confirmed T4 prefix causal uses CUTLASS memory-efficient attention; A100 uses actual `pytorch_flash::flash_fwd_splitkv_kernel` and `aten::_flash_attention_forward`. Four additional forced-Flash-only cases (FP16/BF16 × MHA/GQA) passed numerically and recorded real Flash kernels. Final host-mirror variants report zero scalar extraction in all tested shapes.

Known latency boundary: A100 causal prefix=512 with **missing** host mirrors was 0.6429 ms versus baseline 0.6052 ms (~6.2% slower); the host-mirror path was 0.4248 ms (~1.42x faster). The first run showed a similar fallback regression. Longer-prefix fallback cases improved. Thus reduced query work does not imply every missing-mirror/speculative shape speeds up. Torch versions differ between GPUs, so the table is not a controlled comparison of the two cards.

Baseline `3831e7e0918052be50ef38b3ff62154573e213d7` versus this PR `d9d3a21c4225dbb158eb583cad22710d2c3b0b92`. Only the production attention-backend file is swapped; git diff confirms the remaining change is a unit-test file. The actual model weights, tokenizer, HTTP/SSE server, scheduler, KV cache, and production attention stack run without mocks or source isolation.

- Cold prefill: 544/2080/4128 input tokens, cache flushed before each group, actual `cached_tokens=0` checked.
- Prefix reuse: 512/2048/4096 cached tokens + 32 new input tokens, actual cache-hit metadata checked.
- Four concurrent requests: cached-prefix lengths 256/512/2048/4096; new-input lengths 32/48/64/80; total inputs 288/560/2112/4176, with both cold and cached groups.
- A separate audit observes actual ragged batching and nonzero prefix reuse. All **17 real extend batches** have existing CPU length/request-index mirrors with correct lengths, `seq_len - prefix_len = extend_len`, and Query row counts. The tracing wrapper is disabled for performance samples.
- **56 natural-stop responses form 28 baseline/PR pairs across 14 unique inputs** (counting and descriptive-summary prompts). All pairs match exactly in generated token IDs and text, and all stop on a real stop token. A 2048-prefix summary has an existing cold/cache wording variation ("five apple and three pear trees" vs "five apple trees and three pear trees"); both baseline and PR produce the same variation in the corresponding paths. This is not a claim that all cold/cached BF16 outputs are identical.
- The **280 timed responses** use greedy fixed-length generation (`max_new_tokens=64`, `ignore_eos=true`). All tokens through the model-config EOS match, but the full forced-64 outputs do **not** all match: 10 cached concurrent responses first differ at zero-based token index 42, after the earlier stop/EOS tokens. Baseline itself already differs between cold/cache in that tail. Original raw outputs and failed strict comparisons are retained; the natural-stop test above independently checks normal outputs. No blanket exact-64-token accuracy claim is made.

Medians from ABBA server order (baseline/PR/PR/baseline), with per-shape warmup excluded, 5 shuffled repetitions per server block: **10 samples per variant per scenario**, 160 timed groups total. Client TTFT measures request submission to the first SSE event containing a generated token, including tokenization, scheduling and HTTP; concurrent TTFT is the mean of the four requests within a group. Output throughput is total output tokens divided by the complete group wall time, including prefill and decode. Model loading/JIT warmup are excluded.

Observed concurrent TTFT reductions are ~8.9% cold and ~6.3% cached; complete-request throughput remains essentially flat (~0–1.1% change). Small changes are not claimed statistically significant. This model has **6 full-attention layers on torch_native and 18 GDN layers on Triton**; decode is unchanged by this PR. These measurements support a modest end-to-end TTFT benefit, not the attention-function speedups translating into whole-model throughput gains. Dense/SWA, speculative, multimodal, and distributed integration remain outside this real-model run.

Text-only loading uses the public `--json-model-override-args '{"language_model_only":true}'` configuration supported by this revision's model loader. Its dedicated `--language-model-only` flag rejects Qwen3.5 in its architecture allowlist, so that flag is not used; vision weights are skipped by the existing loader. All remaining server arguments are in the reproducible harness below.

### Dense GQA model comparison: Qwen3-0.6B (Google Colab, 2026-10-10)

**Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B**, revision `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`: 28 full-attention layers, 16 Q / 8 KV heads, all using torch_native. Same full-serving ABBA protocol as above: 10 samples per variant/case, 160 timed groups, 280 timed requests; per-shape warmup and model loading excluded. Cached single-request TTFT is reduced by **3.6% / 8.2% / 17.2%** at 512/2048/4096-prefix tokens; concurrent cold/cached TTFT by **21.8% / 19.2%**. The dense model shows larger TTFT benefits than the hybrid model in the longer-prefix/concurrent cases. This is a within-model baseline/PR comparison, not a controlled cross-model throughput comparison.

The original ABBA full-response throughput is **1.3–2.6% lower**, despite lower TTFT. Its slower segment is after the first token; constructor, forward-metadata init, and both decode methods have identical ASTs between baseline and PR. That alone does not establish a noise explanation, so a separate control below tests the same server process.

**Same-process diagnostic control:** load the two unmodified production extend implementations, select one once per ordinary-extend batch, and keep the model, scheduler, cache, decode methods and service process fixed. Alternate AB/BA order for 8 rounds in two representative cached cases (32 timed groups; 8 samples/variant/case), after warmup. This additional wrapper is diagnostic instrumentation and is not included in the production ABBA table.

In this control, cached-4096 and concurrent-cached TTFT decrease by **18.2% / 21.1%**, while throughput changes by only **+0.2% / +0.5%**. The original throughput decline does not reproduce in this fixed-process control. This supports process/VM variation as a contributor, but does not prove the cause of the original 1.3–2.6% decline or establish a significant throughput gain. Both datasets are retained; the supported benefit is prefill/TTFT, with essentially unchanged complete-request throughput in the control.

## Summary

Torch-native extend pads Query to the full KV length, computes cached-prefix Query rows, and discards their outputs. Run SDPA only for new tokens, and reuse existing CPU length/request-index mirrors to avoid scalar synchronization.

```text
before: SDPA([unused prefix Query; new Query], cached KV) → discard prefix output
after:  SDPA(new Query, cached KV, prefix-aligned causal bias) → new output
```

- Ordinary prefix causality uses PyTorch `causal_lower_right`; eligible fused CUDA dispatch is retained. Sliding-window masks use absolute Query offsets. Prefix-free causal attention retains `is_causal=True`.
- CPU mirrors are used only for non-speculative extend. Missing/length-mismatched mirrors fall back per field; no new device-to-host transfer or persistent batch state is introduced. Decode is unchanged.
- Tests separate input preparation, independent reference math, and backend execution, with public ENCODER_ONLY coverage as well as causal/cross-attention paths.

## Evidence

Rebased onto `3831e7e091` (main on 2026-10-09).

- **Before:** the query-workload regression fails on latest main; the CPU-metadata profiler regression fails on the prefix-only intermediate commit.

SDPA executes real math, checked against independent matmul/softmax results.
- Fresh MPS FP16 validation: all **21 scenarios** (prefixes 0/512/2048/4096; causal/window/noncausal; 16 new tokens, plus 9 three-request ragged cases with 128/127/126 new tokens) match latest main exactly and pass an independent CPU float32 reference at `atol=rtol=0.002`. The 10 new test methods also pass on **PyTorch 2.13.0** as an additional compatibility check. Pre-commit passes on both changed files.

+            causal=causal,
+            window=window,
+            cross_attention=cross_attention,
+            scale=0.3,
+        )
+        expected = _reference_attention(
+            **options,
+            req_indices=req_indices,
+            prefix_lens=prefix_lens,
+            extend_lens=extend_lens,
+            seq_lens=seq_lens,
+            encoder_lens=encoder_lens,
+        )
+        output, query_lengths, scalar_reads = _run_attention(
+            **options,
+            batch=batch,
+            public_forward=public_forward,
+            profile_metadata=profile_metadata,
+        )
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(output, expected, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5)
+        # Cached prefix queries must not be recomputed and discarded by SDPA.
+        self.assertEqual(query_lengths, list(extend_lens))
+        return scalar_reads
+
+    def test_cpu_metadata_avoids_scalar_reads(self):
+        """Existing host mirrors remove device scalar reads from public extend."""
+        options = dict(
+            prefix_lens=(0, 5, 8),
+            extend_lens=(3, 4, 1),
+            public_forward=True,
+            profile_metadata=True,
+        )
+        self.assertGreater(self._check_attention(**options), 0)
+        for mode in (ForwardMode.EXTEND, ForwardMode.MIXED):
+            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
+                self.assertEqual(
+                    self._check_attention(
+                        **options, cpu_metadata=True, forward_mode=mode
+                    ),
+                    0,
+                )
+
+    def test_optional_cpu_metadata(self):
+        """Missing mirrors and an unpadded encoder mirror retain correct slicing."""
+        for mirrors in (True, "partial", "unpadded_encoder"):
+            for cross_attention in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(mirrors=mirrors, cross_attention=cross_attention):
+                    self._check_attention(
+                        prefix_lens=(2, 5),
+                        extend_lens=(3, 1),
+                        encoder_lens=(7, 4),
+                        causal=not cross_attention,
+                        cross_attention=cross_attention,
+                        public_forward=True,
+                        cpu_metadata=mirrors,
+                    )
+
+    def test_speculative_modes_ignore_stale_cpu_metadata(self):
+        """Speculative device metadata can change independently of host mirrors."""
+        for mode in (ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY, ForwardMode.DRAFT_EXTEND_V2):
+            with self.subTest(mode=mode):
+                self._check_attention(
+                    prefix_lens=(2, 5),
+                    extend_lens=(3, 1),
+                    public_forward=True,
+                    cpu_metadata="stale",
+                    forward_mode=mode,
+                )
+
+    def test_causal_prefix_and_ragged_batch(self):
+        """A rectangular causal mask must align each query after its own prefix."""
+        self._check_attention(prefix_lens=(0, 3, 7), extend_lens=(4, 2, 1))
+
+    def test_zero_extend_rows(self):
+        """Padding rows contribute no queries and preserve later request offsets."""
+        for public_forward in (False, True):
+            for window in (None, 2):
+                with self.subTest(public_forward=public_forward, window=window):
+                    self._check_attention(
+                        prefix_lens=(0, 5, 3),
+                        extend_lens=(0, 2, 0),
+                        window=window,
+                        public_forward=public_forward,
+                        cpu_metadata=public_forward,
+                    )
+
+    def test_sliding_window_prefix(self):
+        """Window edges use absolute query positions even when the prefix is omitted."""
+        for window in (0, 2, 20):
+            with self.subTest(window=window):
+                self._check_attention(
+                    prefix_lens=(0, 5, 8), extend_lens=(3, 4, 1), window=window
+                )
+
+    def test_noncausal_prefix(self):
+        """Noncausal queries retain access to future keys after removing padding."""
+        for public_forward in (False, True):
+            with self.subTest(public_forward=public_forward):
+                self._check_attention(
+                    prefix_lens=(0, 4),
+                    extend_lens=(3, 2),
+                    causal=False,
+                    public_forward=public_forward,
+                    cpu_metadata=public_forward,
+                )
+
+    def test_encoder_decoder_self_attention(self):
+        """Decoder self attention must skip encoder cache slots for each request."""
+        self._check_attention(
+            prefix_lens=(2, 5),
+            extend_lens=(3, 1),
+            encoder_lens=(7, 4),
+            public_forward=True,
+        )
+
+    def test_cross_attention(self):
+        """Decoder queries attend to encoder keys of an independent sequence length."""
+        self._check_attention(
+            prefix_lens=(3, 2),
+            extend_lens=(2, 4),
+            encoder_lens=(7, 3),
+            causal=False,
+            cross_attention=True,
+            public_forward=True,
+        )
+
+    def test_cache_dtype_conversion(self):
+        """Query and cache dtypes may differ; conversion must preserve the output."""
+        self._check_attention(
+            prefix_lens=(6,),
+            extend_lens=(2,),
+            num_kv_heads=4,
+            cache_dtype=torch.float16,
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

@ch-wan @Fridge003 could you review this torch-native extend optimization and help enable the registered dense/SWA CI? The current CI gate requires `run-ci`; the GPU jobs were skipped.

I added real HTTP/SSE A100 comparisons for both Qwen3.5-0.8B (6 full-attention + 18 GDN layers) and Qwen3-0.6B (28 full-attention GQA layers), against the same fixed main baseline. Each model has 160 timed groups / 280 timed responses in ABBA order and 28 exact baseline/PR natural-stop output pairs. Actual prefix hits, ragged concurrent batches, and existing CPU metadata are checked.

For Qwen3, cached-4096 TTFT drops 117.30 → 97.13 ms (17.2%); concurrent cached TTFT drops 196.84 → 159.13 ms (19.2%). Qwen3.5 has smaller cached TTFT reductions (1.6–4.2% single-request, 6.3% concurrent).

The original Qwen3 ABBA throughput was 1.3–2.6% lower, so I retained it and added a same-process alternating control: TTFT improves 18.2% / 21.1% in the two cached cases, while throughput is essentially flat (+0.2% / +0.5%). The PR claims a prefill/TTFT benefit; it does not claim an overall decode/throughput speedup. Forced post-EOS tails and existing cold/cache wording differences are documented, separately from the exact normal-output checks.

Both result tables, limitations and reproduction scripts are in the updated Evidence section. Thanks!
